commits.message:
fix(markdown): list items hold blocks, h1 is centred, inline links parse fully (rich-markdown-ht8e)

A list item is now a container, tokenized as Markdown of its own under its
content column, the way a quote already was: fences, quotes and nested lists
inside an item survive, nesting is drawn from the parent's text column, a
number short of the content column is a sibling, numbering counts on from the
first item, and a marker four columns in is indented code.

Lazy continuation is one rule for quotes and items. Outside a container no
paragraph is open, so any list item ends it: "> a\n2024. b" now opens a list,
as CommonMark and Rich read it.

h1 centres per row and h2+ stay left; the heading style is the text's own,
so centring pads beside it. Inline text is parsed rather than matched: link
URLs keep balanced parentheses, link text is inline Markdown, and an image
draws as Rich's ImageItem does.

fix(color)!: one hex grammar behind every hex parser, and a ColorSystemName union (rich-color-2qev) (#296)

* fix(color): one hex grammar behind every hex parser, and a ColorSystemName union for every colorSystem (rich-color-2qev)

parseRgbHex/parseRgbaHex validated nothing: parseRgbHex("1g0000") returned red=1.
They, and parseHexColor (moved to core/color.ts beside them), are now one
private grammar check at the lengths each admits, throwing ColorParseError
naming the input. ColorSpec.parse, theme data, resolveColorRef and the template
colour functions route through them; their own regexes and the exported
HEX_COLOR_RE are gone. resolveColorRef still throws ColorRefError, wrapping.

ColorSystemName is derived from the depth table it names. resolveColorSystem
no longer accepts FORCE_COLOR values or TERM names ("1", "vscode") through the
env table it shared.

* fix(color): the environment's colour vocabulary is its own Map; hex grammar text read off the admitted lengths (rich-color-2qev)

ENV_DEPTHS no longer spreads the ColorSystemName table, so FORCE_COLOR=none or
TERM=truecolor is an unknown env value, and as a Map a value naming an
Object.prototype member (FORCE_COLOR=constructor) is unknown rather than a
function returned as a depth.
